newsitem.title: BURMA: Rangoon, Bangkok pledge closer ties.
newsitem.headline: Rangoon, Bangkok pledge closer ties.

text.p: Burma and Thailand on Saturday pledged to expand bilateral trade, land and air links, as well as joint border development at the end of an official visit by Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh.

The Burmese military government also made a goodwill gesture by turning over to Thailand a major drug suspect wanted by Thai and U.S. authorities for his alleged involvement in a 486 kg (nearly 1,070 lb) heroin shipment seized in California in 1991.

A statement issued by the two countries said Thailand backed Rangoon's membership in the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) despite protests by human rights groups seeking greater political freedom for opponents of the ruling Burmese military regime.
Human rights groups have criticised Chavalit's visit and condemned Thailand's constructive engagement policy to Burma.

But the joint statement said Thailand and Burma "expressed the view that each country has the right to pursue its own path of national development and that outside interference would be counter-productive."

Rangoon handed over to Thai officials Li Yun Chung, alias Phongsak Rojanasakul, who had fled to Burma after jumping bail in March while he awaited a Thai decision on his extradition to the United States.
Li, a close aide of once opium warlord Khun Sa, was the main suspect in a drug haul worth up to $122 million.
Thai sources said the drug suspect was put on the same plane that flew Chavalit's delegation back to Bangkok on Saturday.

Burma and Thailand agreed to expedite border demarcation, raise two-way commercial air traffic on the Rangoon-Bangkok route to 7,000 seats a week from next October, and future Thai purchase of Burmese electricity from 2010.
